# Architecture Component Description — SGIA Capstone
### ArchiMate View generated by `sgia_arquitectura_capstone_v2.ajs`
Capstone Case — National Health Authority (Ente Rector del Sector Salud)

This document describes, in plain language and with its regulatory backing, each element of the **" Agentic ISO 42001 Architecture"** view: 5 Application Functions (the 4 flow layers + the cross-cutting layer), 13 Application Components, 1 Application Interface, and 1 Application Collaboration, along with the relationships that connect them. This is the reference architecture for the capstone's three technical capabilities (Model Router, Run Engine, Audit Repository) described in `Caso_Estudio_Capstone_Ministerio_Salud.md`.

**View design principle:** each component does not merely make the system work — it produces, as a byproduct of its technical function, the evidence an ISO/IEC 42001 auditor requires. That is why every element states, in addition to what it does, which ISO/IEC 42001 clause or control it supports as evidence.

---

## 1. The four behavioral layers (Application Function)

Modeled as **Application Function** — automated behavior, not structure — because the original diagram described them as a process flow (numbered arrows), not as structural boxes.

### 1.1 Bounded Contextualization
Determines what information each agent can see and where it comes from, before any reasoning begins. Realized by the context- and corpus-management components (section 2.1).

> **ISO/IEC 42001 evidence:** supports Annex A.7 (Data for AI systems) — provenance (data lineage), quality, and segmentation of the corpus that feeds the AIMS.

### 1.2 Agent Reasoning
Decides which model resolves each task and coordinates the intermediate steps of an agentic flow. Realized by the model router and the multi-agent orchestrator (section 2.2).

> **ISO/IEC 42001 evidence:** supports Annex A.6 (AI system life cycle) and A.9 (Use of AI systems) — records which model resolved each task and why, traceable to Policy as Code.

### 1.3 Deterministic Verification
Validates every result produced by the reasoning layer against explicit rules before it advances, leaving an immutable audit trail of the decision. Realized by the components in section 2.3.

> **ISO/IEC 42001 evidence:** the technical evidence an auditor asks for first — supports Clause 9.2 (Internal audit, under ISO 19011) and the verification control within Annex A.6.

### 1.4 Operational Governance
Manages human approval (HITL — human-in-the-loop) for decisions flagged as reserved by policy, and injects that decision as binding for the flow. Realized by the components in section 2.4.

> **ISO/IEC 42001 evidence:** supports Annex A.3 (Internal organization — roles and responsibilities) and A.9 (Use of AI systems); documents that a person, not the system, made the reserved decision (human-in-command, ISO/IEC 22989).

### 1.5 Policy Governance *(cross-cutting)*
Cross-cutting behavior that audits and controls budget, anonymizes sensitive data, and filters unsafe instructions, applied across all four flow layers — not on a single one. It is realized by the Application Collaboration in section 3.

> **ISO/IEC 42001 evidence:** cross-cuttingly supports Clause 7.1 (Resources), Annex A.7 (Data for AI systems), and A.9 (Use of AI systems) — no layer falls outside the governance scope.

---

## 2. The structural components by layer (Application Component)

### 2.1 Layer 1 — Bounded Contextualization

| Component | What it does | ISO/IEC 42001 evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Minimum Context Package Manager (PC-nnn)** | Assembles the minimum context package (PC-nnn) delivered to an agent for a specific task, avoiding exposure of the full corpus. | Each PC-nnn is a record of what information an agent received and when — evidence of data minimization under Annex A.7. |
| **Anchor-Based Input Manager** | Resolves which documents or records ("anchors") are the authorized source of context for a given request. | Documents the provenance (data lineage) required by Annex A.7 — which authorized source the data the agent used came from. |
| **Segmented Corpus Manager** | Keeps the knowledge corpus partitioned by domain or sensitivity, so access can be governed per segment. | Supports the data-access-by-sensitivity control in Annex A.7, and allows the AIMS scope to be bounded by corpus segment. |

### 2.2 Layer 2 — Agent Reasoning

| Component | What it does | ISO/IEC 42001 evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Proprietary and Small Model Router** | Decides, per request, whether a small local model or a proprietary commercial model resolves the task, based on cost, sensitivity, and latency. | Each routing decision is logged as evidence of Policy as Code (Annex A.6) — which model was used and under what criterion. |
| **Multi-Agent Orchestrator** | Coordinates the execution of several agents and their intermediate steps for a single task, exposing its calls through MCP contracts. | Documents the sequence of steps of an agentic flow, traceable to the process risk assessment under ISO/IEC 23894 (Annex A.6). |
| **MCP Interface (Model Context Protocol)** *(Application Interface)* | Standard contract through which the Multi-Agent Orchestrator exposes and consumes tools and context in a traceable way. | Being an explicit, versioned contract, it supports the integration traceability required by Annex A.10 (Relationships with third parties) when the model or tool is external. |

### 2.3 Layer 3 — Deterministic Verification

| Component | What it does | ISO/IEC 42001 evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Dependency Graph Validator** | Verifies that the steps of an agentic flow were executed in the order and with the dependencies the task requires. | Technical proof of operational control under Annex A.6 — that the system did what its design says it should, in the correct order. |
| **"When → Then" Rules Engine** | Evaluates each result against explicit business rules before letting it advance to the next layer. | The rules themselves are the operational form of institutional policy (Annex A.2) — their version and change history are auditable evidence. |
| **Immutable Audit Log Repository** | Persists, with no possibility of alteration or deletion, every decision and its provenance, as evidence for audit. | This is, literally, the record that Clause 9.2 (Internal audit, ISO 19011) and Annex A.6 require to be kept — without this component, no other control can be demonstrated. |

### 2.4 Layer 4 — Operational Governance

| Component | What it does | ISO/IEC 42001 evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Human Approval Queue (HITL, H-nnn)** | Queues decisions flagged by policy as reserved, pending approval from an authorized person. | Each H-nnn item documents who approved which reserved decision — direct evidence of human oversight under Annex A.3 and A.9. |
| **Binding Decision Injection Engine** | Applies the human decision made on a HITL queue item to the flow, so the system executes it as binding. | Closes the loop on the reserved decision — records that the executed action matches exactly what the person authorized, not what the system would have done alone. |

### 2.5 Cross-cutting layer — Policy Governance

| Component | What it does | ISO/IEC 42001 evidence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Real-Time Financial Budget Control** | Monitors and limits spend on commercial models by request, area, and period, at execution time. | Supports Clause 7.1 (Resources) — demonstrates that AI use stays within the resources allocated and approved by Management. |
| **Automated Anonymization** | Masks or pseudonymizes personal or sensitive data before it leaves one layer for another or for an external model. | Data-protection control required by Annex A.7, applied before the data leaves the governed perimeter — not after. |
| **Cognitive Firewall** | Filters unsafe instructions, prompt-injection attempts, and potentially harmful outputs before they reach the user or the database. | Supports the security control for AI systems in use (Annex A.9) — evidence that unsafe outputs are blocked before the point of impact, not detected afterward. |

**Cross-Cutting Policy Governance** *(Application Collaboration)* — Groups the three components above, which jointly realize policy governance: budget, anonymization, and instruction filtering.

> **ISO/IEC 42001 evidence:** as a collaboration, it is the auditable unit that demonstrates resource, data, and security control operate in a coordinated way across the four layers, not as isolated patches.

## 3. View relationships

| Source | Relationship | Target | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| The 3 Layer-1 components | Assignment | Bounded Contextualization | Each component executes its layer's function |
| The 2 Layer-2 components | Assignment | Agent Reasoning | same |
| The 3 Layer-3 components | Assignment | Deterministic Verification | same |
| The 2 Layer-4 components | Assignment | Operational Governance | same |
| Multi-Agent Orchestrator | Composition | MCP Interface | The Orchestrator owns and exposes the MCP contract |
| MCP Interface | Serving ("via MCP contract") | Model Router | The Router consumes the MCP interface exposed by the Orchestrator to invoke models and tools |
| Bounded Contextualization | Flow ("1. Context Injection") | Agent Reasoning | Sequential process flow |
| Agent Reasoning | Flow ("2. Delivery for Validation") | Deterministic Verification | same |
| Deterministic Verification | Flow ("3. Exception Escalation") | Operational Governance | same |
| Cross-Cutting Policy Governance | Aggregation | Budget Control, Anonymization, Cognitive Firewall | The collaboration aggregates its 3 components |
| Cross-Cutting Policy Governance | Realization | Policy Governance *(function)* | The collaboration realizes the cross-cutting function |
| Policy Governance | Association ("Intercepts and injects policies") | The 4 layer functions | See modeling note below |

> **Modeling note:** *Influence* would have been semantically more precise for the last relationship (policy "influences" each layer), but Archi's relationship validator rejects it between two Application Functions. *Association* is the metamodel's "any-to-any" relationship and is valid here — the label "Intercepts and injects policies" was kept to preserve the original meaning.

---

## 4. Layer-by-layer control traceability (view documentation)

| Layer | Supports |
| --- | --- |
| Bounded Contextualization | Annex A.7 (Data for AI systems): provenance, quality, and segmentation of the corpus |
| Agent Reasoning | Annex A.6 (Life cycle) and A.9 (Use of AI systems): which model decided what, and under which policy |
| Deterministic Verification | Clause 9.2 (Internal audit, ISO 19011) and Annex A.6: the technical evidence an auditor asks for first |
| Operational Governance | Annex A.3 (Internal organization) and A.9: who approved, as a person, each reserved decision |
| Policy Governance (cross-cutting) | Clause 7.1 (Resources), Annex A.7 and A.9: budget, data protection, and security, across all four layers at once |

This traceability is what makes it possible to sustain, session by session throughout the course, the capstone's Statement of Applicability (SoA): every control selected from Annex A has a component in this architecture that implements it — not just a line of text in a policy document.
